item.title: Small-Batch Thread-Sewn Bookbinders Find New Readers Tired of Disposables
item.description:
LEIPZIG — Inside a brick courtyard bindery smelling faintly of linen thread and wheat paste, two restored 1960s sewing machines stitch folded paper signatures into books meant to outlive their first owners.

While mass-market paperbacks rely on brittle hot-melt glues that crack after two readings, independent literary houses report rising pre-order demand for modestly priced Smyth-sewn editions.

Tactile Permanence in Print

Publishers say readers buying fewer physical volumes increasingly favor durable cloth spines, French-fold jackets, and archival wood-free stock over glossy novelty coatings.
